region.text: Upper Volta, the colony 'revived ... with its previous boundaries' on 4 September 1947

ledger.note: 5 August 1960: Upper Volta becomes fully independent from France. 'On 5 August 1960, it attained full independence from France'; it had been 'self-government as the Republic of Upper Volta' since 11 December 1958 ('an autonomous republic in the French community'). Cliopatria starts the row only in 1961.

4 August 1984: Upper Volta becomes Burkina Faso. 'the country was renamed "Burkina Faso" on 4 August 1984 by then-President Thomas Sankara' (the History section gives 2 August 1984 for the change of name and says 'The presidential decree was confirmed by the National Assembly on 4 August 1984'). Same state, land and colour.

region.text: the Agacher Strip, 160 km long, centred on the Beli river in northern Burkina Faso

ledger.note: 25 December 1985: Mali and Burkina Faso fight over the Agacher Strip. 'At dawn on 25 December 1985,' the war began over 'a 160-kilometre-long strip of land along the border in northern Burkina Faso' (infobox '25-30 December 1985'; a first brief armed conflict in 1974 is undated on the page). The region is the researcher's reading of 'northern Burkina Faso' (the Oudalan province); the page names no province.

22 December 1986: the ICJ ends the Agacher dispute. 'the court issued a ruling on the matter by a five-member panel of judges on 22 December 1986'; the war itself had ended with 'an ANAD-brokered ceasefire' on the morning of 30 December 1985.

region.text: the western portion of the Agacher Strip

ledger.note: 22 December 1986: the western part of the Agacher Strip goes to Mali. 'Mali received the more-densely populated western portion and Burkina Faso the eastern section centered on the Beli'; infobox 'Agacher Strip is divided between the claimants'. The page gives no area; the Cliopatria shape follows the modern frontier and is not changed.

wars.name: Agacher Strip War

zones.text: the Agacher Strip, a 160 km strip along the northern border

wars.outcome: Ceasefire on 30 December 1985 after five days (25-30 December); the ICJ divided the strip on 22 December 1986, Mali taking the western portion and Burkina Faso the eastern section around the Beli.
wars.note: A brief armed conflict in 1974 is undated on the page; the OAU created a mediation commission. Casualties 'Over 100 Burkinabe and approximately 40 Malian'; official statistics 48 and 11.

wars.name: Jihadist insurgency in Burkina Faso
wars.outcome: Ongoing: 'A Jihadist insurgency began in August 2015'; 'about 60% of the country under government control' in 2022 after the January coup; the government claimed to have recaptured 40% in 2023, while the bishop of Dori claimed 'around 50% of the country was in the hands of Islamists'.
wars.note: The page gives percentages, not territory or dates for any held area, so no contest or loss event is recorded. The 'to' year is the dataset horizon, not an end.

certainty.note: The page says the Franco-British Convention of 14 June 1898 created the modern borders; the Agacher Strip stretch with Mali was uncertain until the ICJ ruling of 22 December 1986 (soft there before 1987). The page is silent on disputes with Niger and Benin.

notes: Page budget 2 of 2 (Burkina Faso, Agacher Strip War). (1) Cliopatria's row starts in 1961 but independence was on 5 August 1960 and the French Fifth Republic shape holds the land in 1960: a new 1960 keyframe repeats the 1961 outline and the French Fifth Republic dossier (eu-22) should lose the land in 1960 (it holds 1,283 of 1,301 cells). Cliopatria also keeps Niger, Chad, Central African Republic and Gabon in the 1960 French shape. (2) The Agacher Strip is placed in the Oudalan province as the researcher's reading of 'northern Burkina Faso'; the page names no province and gives no area, and the strip is not in the gazetteer (a place 'Agacher Strip' should be added: northern Burkina Faso / Mali border around the Beli river). The pre-1986 owner is taken as Burkina Faso because the page places the strip 'in northern Burkina Faso'. (3) Mali is referred to as 'mali-federation', the slug of Cliopatria's row that continues as the Republic of Mali. (4) Upper Volta's dismemberment ('dismantled on 5 September 1932, being split between the French colonies of Ivory Coast' and, the page's list continues, others) and reconstitution on 4 September 1947 predate the dossier and are recorded here only. (5) The Burkina Faso page is silent on the Agacher dispute, on Niger and Benin disputes and ICJ rulings.
